title: Godot + Opus 5.5 + Blenderkit + ChatGPT for images
author: loudhacker
selftext:
Anyone else use blenderkit? Or find that they should stop building local 3d asset gen pipelines and just use real assets?

I wrote the code using a Claude code subscription, Godot, and a paid subscription to Blenderkit.

  
Blenderkit is pretty slick, most of their assets are free but its a cheap subscription for access to the premium ones too. Some of those 3d models were clutch and way better than trying to tripo generate shit lol. 70% goes to the artists and its like 12 bucks.

Used chat gpt for flat 2d art

  
  
Anyways here's what I made with it, and we're doing closed playtests now!

comments.author: Practical-Acadia-725
comments.body: Wow that’s not how my games look lol

comments.author: thecrownforge
comments.body: I'd use existing assets for things the player sees up close or often. A local generator makes more sense when you need many small variations. Did mixing Blenderkit models and AI 2D art create a style mismatch in the game?

replies.author: loudhacker
replies.body:
I found that having Opus MCP help with 3D models for items was really great and then just iterating based on 2D concepts. And I would use concept art from previous things that I liked as input for the next concept so that I could keep stylistic consistency

Character models seem to be the best thing to get from real artists

replies.author: thecrownforge
replies.body: that split makes sense. items are small enough to iterate on, while characters carry much more of the style. do the item shapes still read clearly during a fight, or mainly when you see them in the inventory?

comments.author: xenquish
comments.body: Its surprising splatoon is the only paintball like game I can think of like this. Or de blob. There should totally be more steam ones
